categories.name: It works
categories.notes:
Build OK (0 errors, 10 warnings, all pre-existing NuGet ImageSharp advisories): 5/5. / returns 200 via a '/' domain on the 'MCP Matters' blogFrontPage, lists both posts as cards with title + excerpt, links work; the front page's rich text block shows escaped HTML: 9/10. Posts return 200 and every block type renders, but richTextBlock (the main body block) outputs escaped markup ('

…') on both posts, because the plain RichTextModel carries an IHtmlEncodedString that a non-Umbraco Razor view HTML-encodes: 6/10. Images: 4 provided Unsplash photos imported into a Blog media folder, served via signed GetCropUrl URLs, all 5 load: 5/5. Domain '/' + en-US on the site page, everything published: 5/5.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 4/8: postListBlock was created after the content (call 129) and never moved, so it sits at the document-type root; blockSettings (a settings element that never renders) is filed in Blocks instead of Data. Block grid 7/7: 'Blog Block Grid' (Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid) on both page types with hero, richText, image, heading, quote and postList blocks plus a shared settings element (color, spacing, anchor). Structure 5/5: siteRoot is the only root type and allows blogFrontPage; blogPost is allowed only under blogFrontPage; templates assigned; camelCase aliases. Hygiene 3.5/5: excerpt is a real property, but posts have no date or listing-image property (the list sorts by CreateDate and shows no date); there is a leftover blank heading block on the front page; and the palette was added to the shipped 'Approved Color' data type instead of a custom one.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Pipeline 7/7: both pages call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"); no custom loops; blockgrid partials untouched. Adapters 6/6: six Components/<alias>.cshtml adapters take BlockGridItem<T>, map to records and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup (postListBlock queries children in the adapter, which is acceptable). ViewComponents 5.5/7: one per block, Default.cshtml views, records in Models/Blocks/; but RichTextModel exposes Umbraco's IHtmlEncodedString, so the component view depends on an Umbraco type (and that is what breaks the rich text output). Conventions 3/5: Program.cs and appsettings untouched, no migrations or services, friendly extensions and GetCropUrl used. Tailwind classes were written, but the frontend build failed ('vite' is not recognized), so wwwroot/dist/site.css doesn't exist (404) and the site is completely unstyled.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes:
Posts 3.5/6: 'Why MCP is awesome' (9 blocks: hero, copy, heading, 3 two-column reasons, image, quote, closer) is on topic and accurate but short, about 350 words. 'MCP + Umbraco: better together' has 5 blocks and roughly 200 words, mostly describing how this demo site was built rather than why MCP is awesome. The images are relevant. The repeated image in post 2 is left to the scoring script. Looks 1/4: with no CSS the pages render in browser defaults (Times, blue underlined links), the hero photo runs full width at native height, the post title appears twice (page header plus hero block), and raw

/ tags are visible in the body text. It doesn't look like a real blog.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel/order 2/3: schema and content went through the umbraco and umbraco-editor MCP servers (109 calls), with no migrations, uSync edits or DB access, and the model stayed in the folder. One Management API shell call (call 187: a Python token login to read a document's urlSegment) failed with a 400 and was read-only. Order deviations: a block type (postListBlock) and grid changes were made after the content, and the Razor was written before the stop/build/restart rather than after it. Report 0.5/2: it discloses the publishing detour and the leftover heading block, but it falsely claims 'npm run build produced wwwroot/dist/' (the build failed and the output was never read), and it doesn't notice that rich text renders as escaped HTML or that the site is unstyled.

summary: GLM 5.3 Flash built an MCP-only blog with a clean Umbraco pipeline (GetBlockGridHtmlAsync → alias adapters → ViewComponents), six sensible blocks, imported Unsplash media and a correct '/' domain. The rendered site is unstyled because the Tailwind build failed unnoticed, and every rich text block prints escaped HTML. Content is thin, one block type is misfiled, and the final report wrongly claims the CSS was built.
strengths: Textbook rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, camelCase alias adapters with no markup, one ViewComponent per block, records in Models/Blocks
All schema and content via the two MCP servers; no migrations and no DB or uSync edits
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs
Domain '/' assigned to the site page under WWW; all content published
Reusable block set with a shared settings element (background color, spacing, anchor)

issues.text:
The rich text block renders escaped HTML ('

…

' visible as text) on / and both posts. RichTextModel holds IHtmlEncodedString and Views/Shared/Components/RichText/Default.cshtml writes it with @text in a plain Razor view, which encodes it.
The site is unstyled: wwwroot/dist/site.css returns 404 because 'npm run build' failed ('vite' is not recognized, no npm install) and the model never checked the background output.
The final report falsely claims 'npm run build produced wwwroot/dist/' and doesn't mention the escaped rich text or the missing styling.
postListBlock element type sits at the document-type root, not in Blocks; it was created after the content and never moved.
blockSettings, a settings element that never renders, is filed in Blocks instead of Data.
Posts are short and post 2 is mostly about how this demo was built; there is no publish-date or listing-image property, and the post list sorts by CreateDate and shows no date.
One shell call to the Management API (a Python token login, read-only, returned 400); schema was changed after the content, and the Razor was written before the build/restart.
The post title renders twice on /why-mcp-is-awesome/ (blogPost.cshtml header plus a hero block repeating it); a leftover empty heading block is on the front page.
